title: Symptoms across Menstrual and Hormonal Contraceptive Cycles: Cyclic Reoccurrence and Impact on Perceived Sport Performance and Training Participation
summary: The aim of this study is to systematically record cycle symptoms in trained women and female athletes over four consecutive cycles and to examine their cyclic reoccurrence as well as their impact on perceived sport performance, perceived exertion, and training participation. In addition, relations with individual hormonal profiles will be analyzed. Furthermore, the participants’ experiences and perceptions with symptom-based cycle monitoring over the study period will be examined. Five different study groups will be included: women with a natural menstrual cycle, women taking the combined oral contraceptive pill, women taking the mini-pill, women with a hormonal IUD, and women with a diagnosed menstrual disorder.
conditions: Cyclic reoccurrence of cycle symptoms and their impact on perceived sport performance, perceived exertion, and training participation in women with an eumenorrheic menstrual cycle and woman under hormonel contraception.

interventions.name: Women with a eumenorrheic menstrual cycle (menstrual cycle length of 21-35 days with more than 9 consecutive periods per year)
Women using combined oral contraceptives (containing ethinylestradiol & levonorgestrel, 21 days pill intake & 7 days intake pause)
Women using progestin-only pills (containing desogestrel, taken daily over 28 days)
Women using hormonal intrauterine devices (containing levonorgestrel)
Explorativ women with diagnosed menstrual disorders

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General: Non-smoker, no chronic or acute injuries, trained (exercises more than 3 times a week)
(1)    Women with an eumenorrheic menstrual cycle or who use a copper-based contraceptive, such as an IUD, copper chain, or copper ball. -> Regular cycle of 21–35 days, at least 9 consecutive periods per year, no hormonal contraception for more than 3 months
(2)    Women taking the combined oral contraceptive pill. -> For more than 3 months, a combination of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel, with a 21-day intake phase and a 7-day intake break
(3)    Women taking the progestin-only pill. -> For more than 3 months, containing desogestrel, with a 28-day intake phase and no intake break
(4)    Women using the hormonal IUD. -> For more than 3 months, containing levonorgestrel
(5)    Women diagnosed with a menstrual cycle disorder.
Exclusion criteria:
see inclusion criteria
